classification_reasons: Spec is not tight: spec.md's Flagged concerns leaves the `class` tag's vocabulary explicitly open for the owner (no controlled vocabulary, acceptance of drift), so 'no open concern' does not hold even though two other flagged concerns are closed with a decision.

Blast radius is not small: the plan's own Risks section names gate/checks.py's new entry_route=="incident" sub-checks as the riskiest step because a mistake there would either block every future incident change at gate (e) or silently stop enforcing the lesson/eval invariant; it also touches a new generated-index writer, two command files, two templates, OPERATING_MODEL.md, and a two-manifest version bump — not a change contained to one module.

Code is not already covered by existing tests: plugin/lessons/index.py is an entirely new module and the three new gate sub-checks are new branches with no prior test coverage; the plan correctly schedules new tests (test_lessons.py, extensions to test_gate.py and test_commands_and_skills.py) rather than relying on anything that exists today.
attempted: Intent: compared spec.md Requirements/Design and plan.md Files-that-change against intent.md's Proposed outcome field-by-field (frontmatter fields, index build/check, maintain fallback, status enum, gate sub-checks, template/OPERATING_MODEL/sdlc.yaml edits, Checkable list) — full coverage, no scope drift; explicitly excludes evals/case.py, detect/**, the frozen sample, matching intent's Affected-users exclusions.

Spec and plan: verified the diff for this phase touches only intent/spec/plan/status/evidence files (no plugin or template source yet), consistent with CLAUDE.md's rule that the plan.md run is read-only and phase (c) is the first run with edit tools; checked plan.md's file list against spec.md's Requirements/Design for completeness (every named file in spec appears in plan's Files that change); checked the two intent open questions carried forward (sharing across projects, eval-case frontmatter) are correctly left to their named owners rather than decided here, and the one question for this design pass (tag order) is answered with reasoning grounded in sdlc.yaml's actual single-metric shape.

Proof: no code exists yet at this phase, so no toolchain evidence is expected; evidence/run-b.json and hook-log.jsonl show only Write access to spec.md/plan.md (test_file_lock, protected_paths, secrets_check, format_on_edit all 'allow', no denies, no guardrail or source-file touches) — consistent with a read-only design pass.

Blast radius: cross-checked every file:line citation spec.md and plan.md make against the actual code — plugin/state/yamlish.py:122-123 (single leading '---' skip), tests/test_policy_skills.py:28 (the SKILL.md frontmatter regex), plugin/gate/checks.py:186-227/205-211 (check_artifacts and its existing entry_route=="incident" branch), plugin/gate/checks.py's CHECKS_BY_PHASE wiring of check_artifacts at phase e, plugin/gate/artifacts.py:33-39/76-88 (SPEC_SECTIONS, REQUIRED_ARTIFACTS/REQUIRED_EVIDENCE), tests/test_scaffold.py:41-47 (marketplace/plugin version cross-check), and the current manifest versions (still 0.3.5, matching the plan's 'bump last' step) — all accurate, no citation points at the wrong code.

Policies: confirmed data-conventions rules 1 and 3 are cited correctly (personal-data classification; migrations meaning stored/queried data, not a markdown convention) to support spec's 'no risk_list item applies' claim; confirmed CLAUDE.md's guardrail list (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, this repo's root sdlc.yaml) does not include template/sdlc.yaml or docs/OPERATING_MODEL.md, so spec's claim that both are ordinary plugin content editable in phase (c) is correct, and the diff itself touches none of the four guardrail files; confirmed decisions 8, 9, 17 and choices 88/126 referenced by intent/spec exist and say what they're cited as saying.

The tests: reviewed plan.md's Proof and Risks sections for whether planned tests could pass with the bug still present — the plan explicitly calls for per-fail-case tests (missing lesson, missing field, missing eval folder, failing check, dangling supersedes, out-of-enum status) rather than one aggregate test, and a dedicated fixture with a `key: value`-shaped body line to catch a frontmatter reader that doesn't stop at the second '---'; this is not a fix-type change so the pre-existing-test-weakening rule does not apply, and no test file is touched in this diff.
